`urlsplit()` is the function that returns five components, and `urlunsplit()` reverses it.

```json
{"facts": {"split": "urlsplit", "join": "urlunsplit"}}
```

`urlsplit(url)` breaks a URL into scheme, netloc, path, query and fragment. `urlunsplit(parts)` combines the elements of a tuple returned by `urlsplit()` back into a complete URL string. The doc text I read confirms the `urlunsplit` description, but I didn't open the section that lists the five components, so that list is from my own knowledge of the API.

The related `urlparse()` returns six components, because it also splits out the path parameters, and `urlunparse()` reverses it.

Source: `library/urllib.parse.rst`
